olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: On a given circle, six points $A,B,C,D,E,$ and $F$ are chosen independently and uniformly with respect to arc length. Determine the probability that the two triangles $ABC$ and $DEF$ are disjoint, i.e., have no common points.

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement:
Prove that the roots of
$$x^5+ax^4+bx^3+cx^2+dx+e=0$$
cannot all be real if
$$2a^2<5b.$$
statement_note: Inequality visually verified from PDF image because OCR superscripts can be unreliable.

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Each set of a finite family of subsets of a line is a union of two closed intervals. Moreover, any three of the sets of the family have a point in common. Prove that there is a point which is common to at least half the sets of the family.

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Six segments $S_1,S_2,S_3,S_4,S_5,$ and $S_6$ are given in a plane. These are congruent to the edges $AB,AC,AD,BC,BD,$ and $CD$, respectively, of a tetrahedron $ABCD$. Show how to construct a segment congruent to the altitude of the tetrahedron from vertex $A$ using straightedge and compass.

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Consider an open interval of length $1/n$ on the real number line, where $n$ is a positive integer. Prove that the number of irreducible fractions $p/q$, with $1\le q\le n$, contained in the given interval is at most $(n+1)/2$.
